architecture.mechanism: Low-temperature hardening of materials shifts baseline mechanical response (increased torque/force, decreased rotational speed), and a change-point detection algorithm with Z-score normalization can identify the transition between normal and frozen/hardened states in real time.
architecture.intervention: Instrument the 8-speed automatic transmission (2020 Kia Sorento V6) with a cold-state detection algorithm that runs Z-score normalization on live shift-hydraulic pressure, torque-converter slip, and solenoid current signals, then uses change-point detection to flag the cold-engine state at startup; use that flag to apply a cold-mode shift map (higher line pressure, delayed upshifts, modified torque-converter lockup schedule) until the algorithm detects the warmed-state change-point.
architecture.expected_effect: Erratic cold-shift behavior is reduced because the transmission controller explicitly recognizes the cold-soak condition and applies a calibrations map matched to cold-fluid viscosity, instead of using the warm-state shift logic that causes the reported harshness and inconsistency.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument 6 vehicles (3 baseline TCM calibration, 3 with the cold-state algorithm and cold-mode map) with CAN data loggers; perform 20 cold-soak shifts per vehicle (ambient <0 °C, soak >8 h); compare cold-to-warm shift-event timing variance, shift jerk (m/s^3), and number of complaints-grade shift events between the two groups using a paired t-test (alpha = 0.05); if the algorithm group does not show a statistically significant reduction in variance and jerk versus baseline, the mechanism is falsified for this application.
